proof.text: Construct the base-changed polynomial map by the tensor-product map and the canonical polynomial/tensor-product ring equivalence. Right exactness gives surjectivity and identifies its kernel with the extension of the original kernel. The square commutes on coefficients and variables. Use Algebra.TensorProduct.map_surjective, MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv, and Algebra.TensorProduct.rTensor_ker directly; Algebra.Presentation.baseChange is not invoked.

The two quotient rings by the extended prime ideals are isomorphic, carrying the induced primes to one another, so their heights agree by RingEquiv.height_map. Both vertical maps are flat and all rings are Noetherian; apply Ideal.height_eq_height_add_of_liesOver_of_hasGoingDown to both maps and reassociate addition. Flatness is inferred from Module.Flat tensor-product stability over a field, via RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff; faithful flatness is not needed. Noetherianity uses polynomial-ring instances, Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing, and isNoetherianRing_of_surjective.

lean.statement:
theorem polynomial_presentation_height_field_extension
    {k : Type u} {K : Type v} {S : Type w} [Field k] [Field K] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k K] [Algebra k S] (n : ℕ)
    (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k →ₐ[k] S) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    ∃ g : MvPolynomial (Fin n) K →+* (S ⊗[k] K), Function.Surjective g ∧
      ∀ Q : PrimeSpectrum (S ⊗[k] K),
        let q := PrimeSpectrum.comap
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := k) (A := S) (B := K)) Q
        (q.asIdeal.comap f.toRingHom).height + Q.asIdeal.height =
          (Q.asIdeal.comap g).height + q.asIdeal.height

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K/k$ be a field extension, $S$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and
$f\colon k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ a surjective homomorphism of $k$-algebras. Then there is a
surjective ring homomorphism $g\colon K[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S\otimes_kK$ such that for every
prime $Q$ of $S\otimes_kK$, with contraction $q$ to $S$,

$$
\operatorname{ht}\bigl(f^{-1}(q)\bigr)+\operatorname{ht}(Q)=\operatorname{ht}\bigl(g^{-1}(Q)\bigr)+\operatorname{ht}(q).
$$

proof.text: *Construction of $g$.* Let $g$ be the composite of the canonical isomorphism $K[x_1,\dots,x_n]\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\otimes_kK$ with $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_K:k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\otimes_kK\to S\otimes_kK$. By right exactness of $-\otimes_kK$, $g$ is surjective and its kernel is the extension $(\ker f)K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of the kernel of $f$. The square formed by $f$, $g$ and the maps $k[x]\to K[x]$, $S\to S\otimes_kK$ commutes, as one checks on coefficients and variables.

*Heights.* Let $Q$ be a prime of $S\otimes_kK$ with contraction $q$ to $S$, and put $\mathfrak P=f^{-1}(q)$ and $\mathfrak P'=g^{-1}(Q)$; by commutativity of the square, $\mathfrak P'$ lies over $\mathfrak P$. Since $\ker f\subseteq\mathfrak P$, $f$ induces $k[x]/\mathfrak P\cong S/q$, and therefore the fibre rings $K[x]/\mathfrak PK[x]\cong(k[x]/\mathfrak P)\otimes_kK$ and $(S\otimes_kK)/q(S\otimes_kK)\cong(S/q)\otimes_kK$ are isomorphic, the isomorphism carrying the prime induced by $\mathfrak P'$ to the prime induced by $Q$. Hence these two primes of the fibre rings have the same height $h$.

Both maps $k[x]\to K[x]$ and $S\to S\otimes_kK$ are flat (base change of the flat extension $k\to K$ of fields), so they satisfy going down, and all four rings are Noetherian ($k[x]$ and $K[x]$ by the Hilbert basis theorem, $S$ and $S\otimes_kK$ as their quotients). For a flat map of Noetherian rings, the height of a prime equals the height of its contraction plus its height in the fibre ring. Thus $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak P')=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak P)+h$ and $\operatorname{ht}(Q)=\operatorname{ht}(q)+h$, and hence $\operatorname{ht}(f^{-1}(q))+\operatorname{ht}(Q)=\operatorname{ht}(g^{-1}(Q))+\operatorname{ht}(q)$.
